```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(survey)
library(WeMix)
library(labelled)
library(sf)
library(Rrepest)

teacher_path <- "~/Desktop/TALIS/ttgintt4.rds"
principal_path <- "~/Desktop/TALIS/tcgintt4.rds"

teacher_data <- readRDS(path.expand(teacher_path))
principal_data <- readRDS(path.expand(principal_path))
```

```{r}
# 2. SCHOOL-LEVEL VARIABLES

schools <- principal_data %>%
  filter(IDPOP == 2) %>%
  transmute(

    CNTRY,
    IDSCHOOL,

    # TC4G28A: # question askes is supporting the integration of digital resources and tools for teaching
    # 1 = Never or rarely
    # 2 = Sometimes
    # 3 = Often
    # 4 = Very often
    digital_leadership = case_when(
      TC4G28A %in% 1:4 ~ as.numeric(TC4G28A),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # TC4G40E = shortage/inadequacy of digital technology
    # TC4G40F = insufficient internet access
    # Higher score = greater shortage
    digital_shortage = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        as.numeric(TC4G40E),
        as.numeric(TC4G40F)
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),

    # Principal MGCFA scales
    instructional_leadership = as.numeric(T4PLEADS),
    staff_participation = as.numeric(T4POPPART)
  )
```

```{r}
# 3. MAIN ANALYSIS SAMPLE

q20_vars <- paste0("TT4G20", LETTERS[1:10]) #This looks at question 20, its coding is explained in the papers methodology

teachers_bc <- teacher_data %>%
  filter(
    IDPOP == 2,
    IDTQUEST %in% c(2, 3)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Outcome: Question 21, item G
    no_pl_confirmed = if_all(
      all_of(q20_vars),
      ~ !is.na(.x) & as.numeric(.x) == 4
    ),

    ai_pl_from_routing =
      is.na(TT4G21G) & no_pl_confirmed,

    ai_pl_access = case_when(
      as.numeric(TT4G21G) == 1 ~ 1,
      as.numeric(TT4G21G) == 2 ~ 0,
      ai_pl_from_routing ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Declared need for AI-related professional learning
    ai_need = factor(
      as.numeric(TT4G24G),
      levels = 1:4,
      labels = c(
        "No need",
        "Low need",
        "Moderate need",
        "High need"
      )
    ),

    # Create simple dummy variables; reference group is "No need"
    need_low = as.integer(ai_need == "Low need"),
    need_moderate = as.integer(ai_need == "Moderate need"),
    need_high = as.integer(ai_need == "High need"),

    # TALIS MGCFA scales
    digital_self_efficacy = as.numeric(T4SEDRT),
    information_exchange = as.numeric(T4EXINF),
    professional_collaboration = as.numeric(T4COLES),

    # Well-being/stress scales
    workplace_wellbeing = as.numeric(T4WELS),
    workload_stress = as.numeric(T4WLOADT),
    student_behaviour_stress = as.numeric(T4STBEH),

    # Teacher experience category supplied by TALIS
    teaching_experience = as.numeric(T4TYEXPTT)
  )
```

```{r}
# Merge principal data and centre continuous predictors

main_data <- teachers_bc %>%
  inner_join(
    schools,
    by = c("CNTRY", "IDSCHOOL")
  ) %>%
  mutate(

    # Unique identifiers
    school_id = paste(CNTRY, IDSCHOOL, sep = "_"),
    country_id = CNTRY,

    # WeMix weights following the TALIS User Guide
    w_level1 = TCHWGT / SCHWGTT, #This divides the final teacher weight (TCHWGT) by the school weight used got # calculating the within school teacher weight
    w_level2 = SCHWGTT,
# These weights are calculated as advised by the OECD TALIS data guide 
)
```

```{r}
# 4. SAMPLE CONSTRUCTION

# Step 1:
# ISCED 2 teachers in questionnaire Forms B and C.
# These forms contain both AI-related professional learning and digital self-efficacy variables.

sample_1 <- main_data

main_sample_log <- data.frame(
  step = "1. ISCED 2 teachers in Forms B/C",
  teachers = nrow(sample_1)
)


# Step 2:
# Keep teachers with a valid answer to TT4G21G: reported participation in AI-related professional learning.

sample_2 <- sample_1[
  !is.na(sample_1$ai_pl_access),
]

main_sample_log <- rbind(
  main_sample_log,
  data.frame(
    step = "2. Valid AI professional-learning participation",
    teachers = nrow(sample_2)
  )
)


# Step 3:
# Keep teachers with valid AI professional-learning need: TT4G24G.

sample_3 <- sample_2[
  !is.na(sample_2$ai_need),
]

main_sample_log <- rbind(
  main_sample_log,
  data.frame(
    step = "3. Valid AI professional-learning need",
    teachers = nrow(sample_3)
  )
)


# Step 4:
# Keep teachers with valid teacher-level predictor variables:
# - digital self-efficacy
# - information exchange
# - professional collaboration
# - teaching experience

sample_4 <- sample_3[
  complete.cases(
    sample_3$digital_self_efficacy,
    sample_3$information_exchange,
    sample_3$professional_collaboration,
    sample_3$teaching_experience
  ),
]

main_sample_log <- rbind(
  main_sample_log,
  data.frame(
    step = "4. Valid digital self-efficacy, collaboration and experience",
    teachers = nrow(sample_4)
  )
)


# Step 5:
# Keep teachers with valid principal-reported school variables,
# valid multilevel weights, and a school identifier.

sample_5 <- sample_4[
  complete.cases(
    sample_4$digital_leadership,
    sample_4$digital_shortage,
    sample_4$instructional_leadership,
    sample_4$staff_participation,
    sample_4$TCHWGT,
    sample_4$SCHWGTT,
    sample_4$CNTRY,
    sample_4$IDSCHOOL
  ),
]

# Exclude invalid or zero weights.
sample_5 <- sample_5[
  sample_5$TCHWGT > 0 &
  sample_5$SCHWGTT > 0,
]

main_sample_log <- rbind(
  main_sample_log,
  data.frame(
    step = "5. Valid school predictors, weights and IDs",
    teachers = nrow(sample_5)
  )
)


# Final model dataset:
# This is the dataset that should be used for M0, M1, M2 and M3.

main_model_data <- sample_5

# Print the sample construction table
print(main_sample_log)

```

```{r}
# Centre continuous predictors in the final analytical sample
main_model_data <- main_model_data %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    selfeff_c = digital_self_efficacy -
      mean(digital_self_efficacy, na.rm = TRUE),

    exchange_c = information_exchange -
      mean(information_exchange, na.rm = TRUE),

    collaboration_c = professional_collaboration -
      mean(professional_collaboration, na.rm = TRUE),

    leadership_c = digital_leadership -
      mean(digital_leadership, na.rm = TRUE),

    shortage_c = digital_shortage -
      mean(digital_shortage, na.rm = TRUE),

    instr_lead_c = instructional_leadership -
      mean(instructional_leadership, na.rm = TRUE),

    staff_part_c = staff_participation -
      mean(staff_participation, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    selfeff_x_leadership = selfeff_c * leadership_c,
    selfeff_x_shortage = selfeff_c * shortage_c,
    selfeff_x_high_need = selfeff_c * need_high
  )

centred_variables <- c(
  "selfeff_c",
  "exchange_c",
  "collaboration_c",
  "leadership_c",
  "shortage_c",
  "instr_lead_c",
  "staff_part_c"
)

colMeans(
  main_model_data[, centred_variables],
  na.rm = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
# 4.1 TEACHING-EXPERIENCE VARIABLES
# teaching_experience comes from TALIS variable T4TYEXPTT:
# 1 = Five years or less
# 2 = 6–10 years
# 3 = 11–20 years
# 4 = More than 20 years
# Teachers with five years or less are the reference group.



# First create a readable experience-group variable.

main_model_data$experience_group <- NA_character_

main_model_data$experience_group[
  main_model_data$teaching_experience == 1
] <- "0_5_years"

main_model_data$experience_group[
  main_model_data$teaching_experience == 2
] <- "6_10_years"

main_model_data$experience_group[
  main_model_data$teaching_experience == 3
] <- "11_20_years"

main_model_data$experience_group[
  main_model_data$teaching_experience == 4
] <- "20plus_years"


# Turn the text labels into an ordered category variable.

main_model_data$experience_group <- factor(
  main_model_data$experience_group,
  levels = c(
    "0_5_years",
    "6_10_years",
    "11_20_years",
    "20plus_years"
  )
)


# Create the three variables used in the regression.
#
# For the reference group, 0–5 years:
# experience_6_10 = 0
# experience_11_20 = 0
# experience_20plus = 0

main_model_data$experience_6_10 <- ifelse(
  main_model_data$experience_group == "6_10_years",
  1,
  0
)

main_model_data$experience_11_20 <- ifelse(
  main_model_data$experience_group == "11_20_years",
  1,
  0
)

main_model_data$experience_20plus <- ifelse(
  main_model_data$experience_group == "20plus_years",
  1,
  0
)


# Check the experience distribution.

table(
  main_model_data$experience_group,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

table(
  main_model_data$teaching_experience,
  main_model_data$experience_group,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
```

```{r}
# 5. DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS: MAIN SAMPLE

# Variables used in the descriptive tables
continuous_vars <- c(
  "digital_self_efficacy",
  "information_exchange",
  "professional_collaboration",
  "digital_leadership",
  "digital_shortage",
  "instructional_leadership",
  "staff_participation"
)

variable_labels <- c(
  "Digital self-efficacy",
  "Information exchange",
  "Professional collaboration",
  "Digital leadership",
  "Digital resource shortage",
  "Instructional leadership",
  "Staff participation in school decisions"
)


# Check the data: these summaries and counts are unweighted
summary(main_model_data[, c("ai_pl_access", continuous_vars)])

table(main_model_data$ai_pl_access, useNA = "ifany")
table(main_model_data$ai_need, useNA = "ifany")
table(main_model_data$teaching_experience, useNA = "ifany")
table(main_model_data$digital_leadership, useNA = "ifany")


# Calculate descriptive statistics for each continuous variable
descriptive_stats <- data.frame()

for (i in seq_along(continuous_vars)) {

  x <- as.numeric(main_model_data[[continuous_vars[i]]])
  w <- as.numeric(main_model_data$TCHWGT)

  # Use the same valid observations for both sets of statistics
  keep <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w > 0
  x <- x[keep]
  w <- w[keep]

  weighted_mean <- weighted.mean(x, w)
  weighted_sd <- sqrt(sum(w * (x - weighted_mean)^2) / sum(w))

  descriptive_stats <- rbind(
    descriptive_stats,
    data.frame(
      variable = continuous_vars[i],
      label = variable_labels[i],
      unweighted_N = length(x),
      unweighted_mean = mean(x),
      unweighted_SD = sd(x),
      weighted_mean = weighted_mean,
      weighted_SD = weighted_sd,
      observed_min = min(x),
      observed_max = max(x)
    )
  )
}


# Weighted descriptive table for the main text
weighted_descriptives <- descriptive_stats[, c(
  "label",
  "unweighted_N",
  "weighted_mean",
  "weighted_SD",
  "observed_min",
  "observed_max"
)]

weighted_descriptives


# Weighted and unweighted comparison table
comparison_table <- descriptive_stats[, c(
  "label",
  "unweighted_N",
  "unweighted_mean",
  "unweighted_SD",
  "weighted_mean",
  "weighted_SD"
)]

comparison_table

# Print the comparison table as LaTeX
cat(knitr::kable(
  comparison_table,
  format = "latex",
  digits = 2,
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c(
    "Variable",
    "N",
    "Unweighted mean",
    "Unweighted SD",
    "Weighted mean",
    "Weighted SD"
  ),
  caption = "Weighted and Unweighted Descriptive Statistics",
  label = "descriptive_comparison"
))


# Overall weighted participation rate
overall_participation <- with(
  main_model_data,
  weighted.mean(ai_pl_access, TCHWGT, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
)

overall_participation


# Weighted participation within each reported-need category
participation_by_need <- main_model_data %>%
  group_by(ai_need) %>%
  summarise(
    teachers = n(),
    weighted_participation = weighted.mean(
      ai_pl_access,
      TCHWGT,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

participation_by_need


# Chart using the same results as the table above
barplot(
  participation_by_need$weighted_participation,
  names.arg = participation_by_need$ai_need,
  main = "AI-related professional-learning participation",
  ylab = "Participation within need category (%)",
  ylim = c(0, 100),
  las = 2,
  cex.names = 0.9,
  col = "darkgreen",
  border = NA
)


# Weighted participation by education system
country_participation <- main_model_data %>%
  group_by(CNTRY) %>%
  summarise(
    teachers = n(),
    weighted_participation = weighted.mean(
      ai_pl_access,
      TCHWGT,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(weighted_participation))

country_participation
```

```{r}
# 6. WEMIX MODELS:
# AI PROFESSIONAL-LEARNING PARTICIPATION AS OUTCOME

# M0: Null model
m0 <- mix(
  ai_pl_access ~ 1 + (1 | school_id),
  data = main_model_data,
  weights = c("w_level1", "w_level2"),
  cWeights = TRUE
)

summary(m0)

m0_results <- data.frame(
  term = names(m0$coef),
  estimate = as.numeric(m0$coef),
  SE = as.numeric(m0$SE)
)

write.csv(
  m0_results,
  "M0_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

```{r}
# M1: Teacher-level model
# Is digital self-efficacy associated with AI professional-learning participation?

m1 <- mix(
  ai_pl_access ~
    selfeff_c +
    need_low +
    need_moderate +
    need_high +
    exchange_c +
    collaboration_c +
    experience_6_10 +
    experience_11_20 +
    experience_20plus +
    (1 | school_id),

  data = main_model_data,
  weights = c("w_level1", "w_level2"),
  cWeights = TRUE
)

summary(m1)

m1_results <- data.frame(
  term = names(m1$coef),
  estimate = as.numeric(m1$coef),
  SE = as.numeric(m1$SE)
)

write.csv(
  m1_results,
  "M1_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
# M3: Test moderation
# selfeff_c : leadership_c
# Does digital leadership change the self-efficacy association?
# selfeff_c : shortage_c
# Does resource shortage change the self-efficacy association?
# selfeff_c : need_high
# Does the self-efficacy association differ for teachers reporting high need compared with the common association specified for the other need categories?

m3 <- mix(
  ai_pl_access ~
    selfeff_c +
    need_low +
    need_moderate +
    need_high +
    exchange_c +
    collaboration_c +
    experience_6_10 +
    experience_11_20 +
    experience_20plus +
    leadership_c +
    shortage_c +
    instr_lead_c +
    staff_part_c +
    selfeff_x_leadership +
    selfeff_x_shortage +
    selfeff_x_high_need +
    (1 | school_id),

  data = main_model_data,
  weights = c("w_level1", "w_level2"),
  cWeights = TRUE
)

summary(m3)

m3_results <- data.frame(
  term = names(m3$coef),
  estimate = as.numeric(m3$coef),
  SE = as.numeric(m3$SE)
)

write.csv(
  m3_results,
  "m3_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

interaction_data <- data.frame(
  label = factor(
    c(
      "Self-efficacy x high need",
      "Self-efficacy x shortage",
      "Self-efficacy x leadership"
    ),
    levels = c(
      "Self-efficacy x high need",
      "Self-efficacy x shortage",
      "Self-efficacy x leadership"
    )
  ),
  estimate_pp = 100 * c(
    -0.000252,
    0.000373,
    -0.000940
  ),
  lower_pp = 100 * c(
    -0.000252 - 1.96 * 0.004249,
    0.000373 - 1.96 * 0.002729,
    -0.000940 - 1.96 * 0.003181
  ),
  upper_pp = 100 * c(
    -0.000252 + 1.96 * 0.004249,
    0.000373 + 1.96 * 0.002729,
    -0.000940 + 1.96 * 0.003181
  )
)

interaction_plot <- ggplot(
  interaction_data,
  aes(y = label, x = estimate_pp)
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = lower_pp, xend = upper_pp, yend = label),
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  labs(
    x = "Interaction coefficient (percentage-point units)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Self-efficacy interactions in Model M3",
    caption = paste(
      "Points: estimates. Lines: normal-approximation 95% confidence intervals.",
      "Each interaction is interpreted in the units of its moderator.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

interaction_plot

ggsave(
  "M3_interactions.pdf",
  plot = interaction_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 3.8
)
```


```{r}
m1_results <- read.csv("M1_results.csv")
m2_results <- read.csv("M2_results.csv")
m3_results <- read.csv("M3_results.csv")

# Format each model's estimates and standard errors
m1_table <- data.frame(
  term = m1_results$term,
  M1 = sprintf(
    "%.4f (%.4f)",
    m1_results$estimate,
    m1_results$SE
  )
)

m2_table <- data.frame(
  term = m2_results$term,
  M2 = sprintf(
    "%.4f (%.4f)",
    m2_results$estimate,
    m2_results$SE
  )
)

m3_table <- data.frame(
  term = m3_results$term,
  M3 = sprintf(
    "%.4f (%.4f)",
    m3_results$estimate,
    m3_results$SE
  )
)

# Match rows by coefficient name
results_table <- merge(
  m1_table, m2_table,
  by = "term", all = TRUE, sort = FALSE
)

results_table <- merge(
  results_table, m3_table,
  by = "term", all = TRUE, sort = FALSE
)

# Keep the ordering used in M3
results_table <- results_table[
  match(m3_results$term, results_table$term),
]

# Blank cells mean the variable was not included
results_table[is.na(results_table)] <- ""

knitr::kable(
  results_table,
  format = "pipe",
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Predictor", "M1", "M2", "M3"),
  caption = "Weighted Multilevel Linear Probability Models"
)
```

```{r}
# ROBUSTNESS CHECKS
# Keep the exact formula you already used.
m3_formula <- formula(m3$call$formula)

# Save the existing output.
capture.output(
  summary(m3),
  file = "robustness_results/M3_original_summary.txt"
)
# Add education-system fixed effects
country_formula <- update(
  m3_formula,
  . ~ . + factor(CNTRY)
)

m3_country <- WeMix::mix(
  country_formula,
  data = main_model_data,
  weights = c("w_level1", "w_level2"),
  cWeights = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
# 1. Create a new scaled teacher weight.

main_model_data <- main_model_data %>%
  group_by(school_id) %>%
  mutate(
    w_level1_scaled = w_level1 * n() / sum(w_level1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# 2. Fit the same M3 using the scaled teacher weight.
m3_scaled <- mix(
  m3_formula,
  data = main_model_data,
  weights = c("w_level1_scaled", "w_level2"),
  cWeights = TRUE
)

summary(m3_scaled)

# 3. Keep the scaled-model coefficients and standard errors.
scaled_results <- data.frame(
  term = names(m3_scaled$coef),
  estimate = as.numeric(m3_scaled$coef),
  SE = as.numeric(m3_scaled$SE)
)

# 4. Compare the three interactions with your original M3.
# m3_results is the original coefficient table saved earlier.
interaction_terms <- c(
  "selfeff_x_leadership",
  "selfeff_x_shortage",
  "selfeff_x_high_need"
)

comparison <- merge(
  m3_results,
  scaled_results,
  by = "term",
  suffixes = c("_original", "_scaled")
)

comparison[
  comparison$term %in% interaction_terms,
]

m3_scaled_results <- data.frame(term = names(m3_scaled$coef),
  estimate = as.numeric(m3_scaled$coef),
  SE = as.numeric(m3_scaled$SE)
)
write.csv(
  m3_scaled_results,
  "m3_scaled_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
    selfeff_x_high_need +
    (1 | school_id),

  data = main_good_samples,
  weights = c("w_level1", "w_level2"),
  cWeights = TRUE
)

summary(m3_good_samples)
```
